blocks.text: BARKPARK TASKS MOBILE · EPIC STATUS REPORT · 2026-07-25

content.value: Barkpark has three clients: the Go TUI + bp CLI, the Phoenix Studio, and the JS SDK surfaces. The Barkpark Tasks epic is building the fourth — a phone. Cloud-exclusive at v1: a plain team member (not an admin) signs in with the Cloud device flow, lands in the right dataset without choosing anything they didn't have to, and gets three surfaces — Tasks, Chat, Papers — as themselves, on a workspace-bound [read,write,chat] token no admin handed them. This paper is the mid-flight status: waves 1 and 2 rounds 1–3 are merged, round 4 has four builders in the air right now, and two human gates stand between here and v1. Every number and screenshot below is from the charter's wave log, the task ledger, or the live emulator evidence — nothing reconstructed from memory.

items.label: wave-1 slices, all merged (exchange, skeleton, js + api unblocks, two spikes)
wave-2 slices merged across rounds 1–3 (revoke, chat tab, push hardening, native reader)
jest suite in apps/mobile after the native reader landed
TS/TSX in apps/mobile — a real app now, not a skeleton
items.value: ~7.8k lines

items.label: fenced builders in flight right now (round 4, dispatched 2026-07-25)
human gates open: a second real Cloud member seat + APNs/FCM credentials

content.value: The product decision was made before the first wave and is inherited, never re-litigated: staged Sweet Spot — the "Operator's Leash" — on Expo/React Native, per the ratified crown paper and its five lanes. The phone is a leash on work already in motion: read the board, triage inside the claim-epoch fence, answer the chat asks that need you, read the papers. The user ratified three calls at founding: (R1) needs-you push ships in v1 as a severable Cloud APNs/FCM relay — slips means v1.1 with zero code debt; (R2) the app-token exchange mints [read,write,chat]; (R3) home is three tabs — Tasks · Chat · Papers — with needs-you badges from the chat rollup.

Two laws bound v1's shape. D19: v1 promises NO editing anywhere — the per-user :write seam is a declared v2 opener, never silently started. D10: chat is workspace-scoped BY DESIGN — a member's chat tab shows the workspace's sessions, because the Operator's Leash is a team tool and the workspace is the floor. The app lives at apps/mobile at repo root with its own blocking CI lane (mobile.yml: typecheck, lint, jest).

Eleven screenshots, all captured on the bpspike Android emulator against live fleet servers — real Cloud sessions, real minted tokens, real boards; no mockups. Two eras are shown and labeled: the SKELETON era (wave-1 close-out, 2026-07-24, when Chat and Papers were honest stubs) and the CHAT-TAB era (wave 2, later that day, after the full chat floor landed). The gitignored originals live in tooling/webview-spike/results/; they were uploaded to this workspace's media library for this report.

Missing on purpose: there are NO screenshots of the shipped native paper reader (af9d64d61) yet. The Papers shots above are the stubs-era tab, labeled as such — this report does not substitute a stub for the shipped reader. A reader evidence pass belongs to the next emulator session.
The founding wave retired the two named risks (member-reachable identity; the long-paper renderer bet) and raised the skeleton, in six file-disjoint slices:

items.value: Member-reachable app-token exchange (87972d0de) — Cloud session-authed proxy + admin-bearer-gated instance mint; the admin token never travels. Live criterion run: 12/12 exchange-mode smoke against guerrilla — mint returned [read,write,chat], workspace-bound, and walked the full journey as that token.

Expo skeleton at apps/mobile (bb875c8c5) — device-flow login, cascade auto-select + MRU (ported from the Go TUI's cloudFleetPick/KnownServers semantics), three stub tabs with honest loading/error/empty states, mobile.yml CI lane.

js unblocks (289b46b1a) — cushioned core size-budget bump (ESM 15.9 < 16.5 KB, CJS 16.59 < 17) + the @barkpark/react heading content[] fix, merged BEFORE the spike so the renderer verdict couldn't be contaminated by blank headings (D12).

API manifest unblocks (87be3b4f2) — D36 closed as an orthogonal capability lattice: chat is a capability, not a rank; a chat-permissioned token projects the chat noun without lifting doc/task tier. Plus fields= manifest flag and production-first dataset ordering.
WebView spike (4fa2cb815) — throwaway harness, 104-block capstone paper, the real 93,449-byte paper-surface.css, numeric thresholds fixed in advance. Verdict below.

Push spike (d4a2ff355, #6030) — device_push_tokens schema (per-user × per-device, platform-tagged), Cloud's first inbound HMAC receiver for the instance chat_blocked webhook (byte-parity t=,v1= scheme, 300 s window), workspace→devices fan-out design. Severability is structural: registration-row-absent — no row, nothing fires; zero flags, zero dead code.

blocks.text: Wave 2 rounds 1+2 — revoke, chat floor, push hardening (3/3, grade A, zero fix rounds)

items.value: App-token revoke path (2a60d013f) — instance DELETE /v1/auth/app-tokens{,/current} + Cloud member-reachable proxy. Live-proven post-deploy: mint → prime 200 → proxy revoke → prime 401; an email sweep killed all 4 tokens accreted by wave-1 smoke runs (revoked_count:4, idempotent re-proof 0). Bonus systems proof: the sweep killed the emulator app's own token mid-session and the app self-healed by re-minting on relaunch — the disposable-credential lifecycle working as designed.

Chat tab full floor (8535cf8b8) — the third sibling client of /v1/chat: reducer.ts/herd.ts ported from internal/chat/{reduce,herd}.go with reviewer-verified line-level semantic parity, send/stream/interrupt/approve-deny over the D14 expoFetch SSE seam, live session list on the D10 floor, rollup badges on a 60 s poll, jest 85/85 (40 new). The builder found and fixed a real leak live: a per-render stream re-subscription (welcome-frame storm), memoized to one welcome per connect.

Push hardening (b2ea6aaf2) — the three spike debts: token cap 4096→1024 counted in BYTES (index-true), webhook replay dedupe via per-job Oban unique insert (reviewer confirmed OSS Oban skips unique enforcement on bulk insert — the switch is load-bearing), and a push_register rate bucket + 20-device cap with revoked-first eviction. Built through a GitHub PR-creation outage without losing work.

blocks.text: Wave 2 round 3 — the native paper reader (shipped 2026-07-25)

content.value: af9d64d61 (PR #6107): the Papers tab became real — paper list + a NATIVE PortableDoc reader with mermaid rendered as isolated WebView islands and a virtualized scroll for long papers. apps/mobile jest now 115/115.

D11, told straight. The charter's rule was numeric: the WebView-vs-native verdict is rendered on real mid-tier Android hardware, and emulator numbers are advisory tripwires only. That binding real-Android verdict NEVER LANDED. What exists is the advisory emulator run: cold-load P50 636 / P95 1041 ms PASS, memory 127 MB PASS, file-vs-inline 0.8x PASS — and scroll FAIL at 43.1 avg fps / 99.3% janky frames. The native fast-path was promoted into round 3 by USER RULING after that FAIL, not by the D11 verdict. The charter's stance stands unamended: emulator numbers stay advisory, and the binding hardware verdict remains an open item.

The epic's proofs follow two habits worth naming. First, the 404-oracle: cross-tenant negatives assert that a wrong-tenant read returns the SAME 404 as a nonexistent id, and the chat floor was proven with ghost-id oracles rather than driving a production session. Second, smoke runs AS the minted token, and over-assertions get inverted rather than deleted: when the /v1/structure leg turned out to pass only on an admin fallback, the fix (#6029, c67255faf) made the member token's 403 the assertion — a 200 in exchange mode now fails loudly as a tier-floor breach. Related probe lesson, recorded so nobody re-trips: /v1/capabilities is an OPEN manifest endpoint (200 for any bearer) — fail-closed proofs must ride a verify-tier route like /v1/tasks/prime.

Push relay BUILD (mob-w2-push-relay-build) — real APNs/FCM adapters behind the Push.Adapter seam, instance webhook-row provisioning, complete up to the credentials HUMAN GATE with Push.Adapters.NotConfigured as the severable default.

Ledger + charter reconciliation (mob-w2-ledger-reconcile) — re-parent orphaned children under the epic root, criteria for the criteria-less backlog, and the round-3 wave-log entry with the D11 miss told straight.

content.value: The epic root carries seven acceptance criteria, written 2026-07-25 and all conservatively unmet — v1 closes without a lie or it doesn't close. What actually stands in the way:

items.value: HUMAN GATE mob-hg-member-seat — guerrilla's Cloud team holds ONE seat, so the plain-member journey has never been walked by an actual second human seat; the minted token is member-shaped at row level, but the live leg needs the seat.
HUMAN GATE APNs/FCM credentials — the relay build stops at the adapter seam until real platform credentials exist; by R1 the fallback is severing push to v1.1 at zero code cost.
The binding D11 real-Android verdict — still the honest open thread behind the reader choice; the emulator scroll FAIL makes it more, not less, worth running.
A physical-device boot — everything so far is the bpspike emulator; the epic's own criteria require at least one boot on real hardware.

Chat-tab era — a session-detail round trip: the message left the phone and the server's reply (an out-of-usage-credits refusal) came back and rendered. The full-floor send against a live agent session remains deliberately deferred to a dev instance — this shot proves the transport, not the floor.

Missing on purpose: there are NO screenshots of the shipped native paper reader (af9d64d61) yet. The Papers shots above are the stubs-era tab, labeled as such — this report does not substitute a stub for the shipped reader. A reader evidence pass belongs to the next emulator session.

What shipped, wave by wave

Wave 1 — proof-first parallel spikes (6/6 merged)

The founding wave retired the two named risks (member-reachable identity; the long-paper renderer bet) and raised the skeleton, in six file-disjoint slices:

• Member-reachable app-token exchange (87972d0de) — Cloud session-authed proxy + admin-bearer-gated instance mint; the admin token never travels. Live criterion run: 12/12 exchange-mode smoke against guerrilla — mint returned [read,write,chat], workspace-bound, and walked the full journey as that token.

• js unblocks (289b46b1a) — cushioned core size-budget bump (ESM 15.9 < 16.5 KB, CJS 16.59 < 17) + the @barkpark/react heading content[] fix, merged BEFORE the spike so the renderer verdict couldn't be contaminated by blank headings (D12).

• WebView spike (4fa2cb815) — throwaway harness, 104-block capstone paper, the real 93,449-byte paper-surface.css, numeric thresholds fixed in advance. Verdict below.
• Push spike (d4a2ff355, #6030) — device_push_tokens schema (per-user × per-device, platform-tagged), Cloud's first inbound HMAC receiver for the instance chat_blocked webhook (byte-parity t=,v1= scheme, 300 s window), workspace→devices fan-out design. • App-token revoke path (2a60d013f) — instance DELETE /v1/auth/app-tokens{,/current} + Cloud member-reachable proxy. Live-proven post-deploy: mint → prime 200 → proxy revoke → prime 401; an email sweep killed all 4 tokens accreted by wave-1 smoke runs (revoked_count:4, idempotent re-proof 0). D11, told straight. The charter's rule was numeric: the WebView-vs-native verdict is rendered on real mid-tier Android hardware, and emulator numbers are advisory tripwires only. That binding real-Android verdict NEVER LANDED. The epic's proofs follow two habits worth naming. First, the 404-oracle: cross-tenant negatives assert that a wrong-tenant read returns the SAME 404 as a nonexistent id, and the chat floor was proven with ghost-id oracles rather than driving a production session. Second, smoke runs AS the minted token, and over-assertions get inverted rather than deleted: when the /v1/structure leg turned out to pass only on an admin fallback, the fix (#6029, c67255faf) made the member token's 403 the assertion — a 200 in exchange mode now fails loudly as a tier-floor breach. In flight right now — round 4, four fenced builders

Dispatched 2026-07-25, file-disjoint, all IN FLIGHT as this report publishes — none of the following is done:

• Tasks tab earns its name (task-dc540e00b27f9ea7) — task detail screen + fence-free triage on the minted member token; the read half shipped in wave 1, the act half is this slice.
• @barkpark/react list emitter (mob-bl-react-list-emitter) — the list emitter drops the dominant {content:[...]} list-item shape: 1,774 of 2,431 live list items render empty on web today. (This paper deliberately uses plain-string list items.)
• Push relay BUILD (mob-w2-push-relay-build) — real APNs/FCM adapters behind the Push.Adapter seam, instance webhook-row provisioning, complete up to the credentials HUMAN GATE with Push.Adapters.NotConfigured as the severable default.
• Ledger + charter reconciliation (mob-w2-ledger-reconcile) — re-parent orphaned children under the epic root, criteria for the criteria-less backlog, and the round-3 wave-log entry with the D11 miss told straight.

Between here and v1

The epic root carries seven acceptance criteria, written 2026-07-25 and all conservatively unmet — v1 closes without a lie or it doesn't close. What actually stands in the way:

• HUMAN GATE mob-hg-member-seat — guerrilla's Cloud team holds ONE seat, so the plain-member journey has never been walked by an actual second human seat; the minted token is member-shaped at row level, but the live leg needs the seat.
• HUMAN GATE APNs/FCM credentials — the relay build stops at the adapter seam until real platform credentials exist; by R1 the fallback is severing push to v1.1 at zero code cost.
• The binding D11 real-Android verdict — still the honest open thread behind the reader choice; the emulator scroll FAIL makes it more, not less, worth running.
• A physical-device boot — everything so far is the bpspike emulator; the epic's own criteria require at least one boot on real hardware.
• Wave 3 (unstarted) — offline cache depth (MMKV/SQLite policies), papers premium polish, TestFlight/internal APK distribution.
